output.explanation: Expanded render-worker because updateFrame and drawFrame hide substantial nested call structure. Its central diagram now follows worker setup, event dispatch and shutdown; frame-update expands snapshot acquisition and cell construction, while frame-present expands drawing and backend completion. call-core and io-worker remain unchanged as surrounding ownership and hand-off context. Checked the pinned checkout's renderer, terminal snapshot, Surface, IO and mailbox paths. Clarified that cursor ticks queue a wake, visibility regain renders before setVisible(), and synchronized output skips snapshot updates rather than every possible draw. Backend detail qualifies the overview's synchronous-presentation shorthand: Metal waits when sync=true; OpenGL ignores that flag and publishes an exported frame for runtime presentation. All existing edges are retained, with moved rendering endpoints redirected.
